GHMC Conducts Surprise Inspections on Non-Compliant Hostels 
 In response to persistent complaints of regulatory non-compliance, GHMC has intensified inspections of private hostels in Ameerpet, Ashok Nagar, and Dilsukhnagar. These establishments, serving students and working professionals, were found violating norms related to food safety (FSSAI), sanitation, fire safety, and urban planning. 
 Key issues include operating without FSSAI and trade licenses, using cellars as kitchens, overcrowding, unhygienic food preparation, and dumping waste in streets. Despite ongoing awareness efforts, many hostels continue to violate essential health and safety standards. 
 To ensure compliance, GHMC formed a Special Task Force to conduct surprise inspections across critical zones. On 23.05.2025, 58 hostels were inspected; 30 notices were issued, 5 hostel kitchens sealed, and penalties totaling ₹2,45,500 imposed under the provisions of the GHMC Act, 1955. 
 Common violations observed during inspections included: 
 • Unclean walls and ceilings 
 • Greasy exhaust systems 
 • Uncovered dustbins 
 • Housefly infestations 
 • Unauthorized kitchens in cellars/parking areas 
 • Food handlers lacking proper hygiene (no hairnets/gloves) 
 • Uneven floors with stagnant water and waste 
 • Cooking and cleaning areas situated too closely 
 • Operation without valid FSSAI and trade licenses 
 • Toilets opening directly into kitchens 
 GHMC will continue strict enforcement to ensure compliance and safeguard public health.
